inputs.share_count_basis: 2,165.4m shares in issue excl. treasury at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 FY2026), FY2025 AR 2,166.7m; dilutive share plans are immaterial (SBC ~S$2.5m/yr). Rounded to 2,166m and held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and there is no non-SBC issuance in prospect.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR share-based payment expenses S$2.5m (C52.SI_Annual_FY2025.txt:10336); no net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes 0). Singapore is an SBC-light market.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:06:00Z SGX regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 7.0% SGD-reported WACC. Flows are translated SGD but ~55% are earned in GBP/AUD/EUR/CNY, so the risk-free rate is revenue-weighted: SGS 10y ~2.4% on the 45% Singapore share and ~4.2% on the overseas share (UK gilt/ACGB) -> ~3.4%. Beta 0.9 (contracted public transport ~0.6-0.7 blended with a structurally challenged taxi book), ERP 5.5% -> cost of equity ~8.4%. Pre-tax cost of debt 3.5% (FY2025 AR average effective rate 3.46%) -> ~2.8% after tax. Target D/V 25% (borrowings + lease liabilities vs market cap) -> 6.95%, rounded 7.0%. Same WACC in all scenarios; risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Property/other lease payments (principal S$61.9m + interest S$10.0m FY2025; S$27.3m + S$4.5m in H1 FY2026) are charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path 1.3% of revenue, and the S$202.7m of IFRS-16 lease liabilities (55.3 current + 147.4 non-current, 30-Jun-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 399.6 less ~S$55m ROU ~= 6.8% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice. 'Lease liabilities from financial institutions' (S$31.2m, vehicle hire-purchase financing, repaid within the borrowings line) are treated as debt and included in total_debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the bridge: flows are 100% consolidated, and the minorities' claim is deducted as an equity_bridge item at ~S$500m. Basis: NCI profit run-rate ~S$32-35m (H1 FY2026 S$15.5m; FY2025 S$41.6m before the Sept-2025 CityCab buy-in) x ~14-15x. Cross-checks: book NCI S$366.1m (30-Jun-2026); market value of the listed minorities (SBS Transit S61.SI S$3.53 and VICOM WJP.SI S$1.72 at 2026-10-23, ~25%/~33% outside holdings) plus unlisted NCI at book is roughly S$550-600m. S$500m sits between book and market.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations -- per dcf-methods routing, CDG is an ordinary operating company (land transport operator), not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco; first valuation, no prior model to match. NET DEBT: borrowings S$1,636.9m + lease liabilities from financial institutions S$31.2m = S$1,668.1m, less cash S$764.5m = S$903.6m (H1 FY2026 balance sheet, 30-Jun-2026). Cash includes SBS Transit's ~S$385m, which is consolidated (and whose minorities are deducted via the NCI bridge). OWNER FCF: reported FY2025 FCF -136.5 (OCF 451.3 - capex 587.8) less SBC 2.5 = -139.0. Interest income is NOT deducted: the group is in net debt, and interest received sits in investing, not OCF, so the reported FCF is already ex-interest. FY2025 FCF is depressed by (i) peak EV/fleet/depot capex (11.6% of revenue vs a 6-10% band FY2020-24) and (ii) a S$139m service-concession-receivable outflow in H1 FY2025 (new Australia/UK bus contracts) -- NEITHER is carried forward: the build is from components, with capex normalising from 9.8% (H1 FY2026 run-rate ~S$500m/yr) to a 7.8% mid-cycle level, above D&A ex-ROU (7.2%) to fund fleet renewal and the electrification targets (90% clean car fleet by 2030, 50% bus by 2030). SBC-zero market in effect (0.05% of revenue): house and street coincide, band_position null. Buybacks are de minimis (S$0.2m FY2025, S$2.7m H1 FY2026 for share plans), so the flat count is a modelling convention CDG does not fund with repurchases -- immaterial at this SBC level. No formal FY2026 guidance ('No forecast or prospect statement has been previously disclosed', H1 FY2026 statements); FY2026 year-1 is anchored on H1 FY2026 (revenue +5.7%, EBITDA margin 13.3% vs 15.4%, taxi operating profit -47%) and the Tampines Bus Package handover from July 2026.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (SBS Transit ~25%, VICOM ~33%, other subsidiaries) at estimated value
equity_bridge.note: Run-rate NCI profit ~S$33m x ~15x; book S$366.1m (H1 FY2026 statements line 186); listed-sub market value ~S$550-600m. See inputs.nci_treatment.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run organic revenue growth (10-yr revenue CAGR 2.1% FY2015-25 incl. COVID; contractual indexation ~2-3% plus international bus/rail wins), not equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges >30% from revenue (9-10%) and EPS (10% 3-yr) CAGRs. Equity is flat because CDG pays out ~80% of earnings and funded the 2023-25 acquisitions (Addison Lee, CMAC, A2B, CityCab buy-in) with debt; the 3-/5-yr revenue CAGRs are M&A- and COVID-recovery-inflated (FY2020 base). Neither is a usable organic growth rate; 3.5% is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs not meaningful: FY2025 owner FCF is negative (-139.0). Owner FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest not in OCF): FY2020 283.2, FY2021 434.5, FY2022 296.6, FY2023 68.8, FY2024 76.2, FY2025 -139.0 -- the decline is capex (6.2% -> 11.6% of revenue) and working capital tied to new concessions, not an operating collapse (EBITDA 540 -> 773). SBC is immaterial (<0.1% of revenue), so reported and owner FCF CAGRs would be identical.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +4.5%: H1 +5.7% (indexation, Metroline London repricing, Victoria contracts, CMAC) less the Tampines Bus Package handed over from July 2026 and a shrinking Singapore taxi fleet. Then 3-4% on public-transport indexation and selective international wins from the >S$17bn pipeline, fading to 2.5%.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2025 15.3%, H1 FY2026 13.3% on the taxi profit collapse. FY2026 13.6%, recovering to 14.8% as the last ~30% of Metroline repricing lands and taxi stabilises at a lower base -- just below FY2025, not back to the 20%+ pre-COVID taxi-heavy mix.
base.capex_rationale: H1 FY2026 capex S$247m (~9.8% annualised) after the FY2025 peak of 11.6%; glides to 7.8% mid-cycle, above D&A ex-ROU, to fund fleet renewal and electrification.
base.tax_rationale: Blended statutory: Singapore 17%, UK 25%, Australia 30%, China 25%; H1 FY2026 effective 20.3%. 21% cash tax on EBIT.
base.wc_rationale: Negative capture: government-contract receivables and service-concession receivables consume cash as the contracted book grows (H1 FY2025 S$139m concession outflow).
base.cap_rationale: 18x unlevered FCF (5.6% FCF yield): contracted, indexed public-transport cash flows justify more than the 12-15x cyclical cap, but the 7%/2.25% Gordon (21.5x) is not granted. Implied terminal EV/EBITDA ~5.2x vs ~5.9x today (ex-lease EV over EBITDA less lease cash).

scenario_narratives.base: Public Transport (~65% of revenue, 97% of contracts >5 years) keeps compounding at indexation plus a handful of international wins; Metroline London repricing completes; the taxi/P2P business stops shrinking at roughly half its FY2025 profit as the hybrid fleet-and-platform pivot and premium/B2B mix offset Grab. Capex steps down from the FY2025 EV/depot peak to a mid-cycle 7.8% and FCF recovers from negative to ~4% of revenue by year 5. Leverage stabilises; the ~80% payout continues but is no longer covered by FCF until ~FY2028.
scenario_narratives.bull: CDG converts a meaningful share of the >S$17bn 2026-28 international bus/rail pipeline (UK franchising in Liverpool/West Midlands/West Yorkshire, Gulf metros, Australian bus), the ~S$850m of 2023-25 acquisitions (Addison Lee, CMAC, A2B) finally integrate and deliver accretion, and a Grab-Gojek consolidation or AV economics (Guangzhou/Punggol robotaxi, 10% AV fleet by 2030) ease point-to-point pressure. EBITDA margin rebuilds to 16% and revenue grows 5-6% for several years.
scenario_narratives.bear: Ride-hailing erosion keeps compounding: the Singapore taxi fleet keeps shrinking, Australia and UK premium (A2B/Addison Lee airline exposure) stay weak, and the acquired businesses need write-downs rather than delivering growth. Contract losses like the Tampines Bus Package handover recur at re-tender, recontracting margins disappoint, and the electrification programme keeps capex at ~8-10% of a slower-growing revenue base. EBITDA margin settles at 12.5% and revenue grows ~2%; debt-funded dividends become a cut.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the taxi segment's operating profit just fell 47% with no proven fix, the M&A has not yet delivered, and leverage has risen ~5x since FY2022 with FCF negative. Base 50% because two-thirds of revenue is long-dated, government-backed and indexed. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (pipeline conversion, M&A integration and a P2P competitive reprieve).
probability_weighted.band_note: DEGENERATE: SBC is ~0.05% of revenue (S$2.5m/yr), so house and street differ by only ~S$0.03/share and band_position divides by that sliver -- the printed value is meaningless. Treat the band as collapsed (SBC-zero market in effect); the price is simply compared with the house weighted IV.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a mid-cycle capex path: the FY2025 negative FCF is a capex and concession-receivable peak, not the earning power of a business with ~S$770m of EBITDA, so the build normalises capex over ~5 years rather than starting from -S$139m. The valuation is a bet on the contracted public-transport franchise carrying a shrinking taxi business; minorities in SBS Transit and VICOM are deducted at roughly market value.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex does not normalise: electrification and new-contract fleet keep capex at 10%+ of revenue, holding FCF near zero for longer
Taxi/P2P decline continues at the H1 FY2026 pace (-47% operating profit) and spreads further into UK/Australia premium
Re-tender losses in Singapore bus (Tampines precedent) or weaker recontracting margins in London
Terminal value is capped at 16x FCF and still ~70%+ of EV; the result is sensitive to the 7% WACC
NCI value estimate (S$500m) is judgment: book S$366m to listed-market ~S$600m spans ~S$0.11/share
